title: Add lammpslib support for kokkos and mliap
body:
Add hooks in `LAMMPSlib` for extra `cmd_args` passed to `lammps.lammps()`, which makes it possible to enable kokkos, and for `LAMMPSlib` to call `activate_mliappy` or `activate_mliappy_kokkos` to support `mliap` `unified` lammps `pair_style`s.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: As far as I can see, these functions link some libraries dynamically.  I think it would be wise to avoid calling the code that performs dynamic linking more than once, which means the user should probably call it in the beginning of main() (like MPI_Init() and similar).

comments.author: noambern
comments.body:
I'm not sure what you're suggesting as the alternative here.  These functions require as an argument the object returned by `lammps()`.  That is only called from `start_lammps()` here, and `start_lammps()` is only called from `propagate()` and `restart_lammps()`.

We could add a flag (similar to `self.started`) so they're only called once, if you think that's better.

comments.author: noambern

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: The most significant change is the ability to add options to the command (`extra_command_args`), whereas the initialization functions can always be called in the way intended by lammps itself, and is hence already "supported".

comments.author: noambern
comments.body: I would argue that they are not, in fact, because the needed functions cannot be called until the object returned by `lammps()` exists, which doesn't happen (in the current overall architecture) until `LAMMPSlib.propagate()` is called, and that  happens inside `LAMMPSlib.calculate()`, by which point it's too late for the user to do anything manually.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
OK, that makes sense: The object isn't visible enough to call custom code on.

However the implementation in lammps looks kind of sketchy (doing the imports in a way that triggers the same library load via custom importlib magic for each lmp object).

In order to solve the problem without getting possibly platform-dependent linking trouble, and without needing to add anything heavy to the test infrastructure, maybe we could allow the user to inject an arbitrary initializer this way:

```
def initialize(lmp):
   lammps.initialize_kokkos(lmp)  # or similar

calc = Lammps(initialize=initialize)
```

This also has the advantage that we don't need to change the code again when lammps adds more initializers.

comments.author: noambern
comments.body:
I'm still not following, sorry.  What is `Lammps`?  Do you mean `LAMMPSlib`, the constructor for the ASE calculator?  Just want to make sure I'm not confusing it with the `lammps` class, which is provided by LAMMPS, not ASE.

Assuming that's what you mean, this action can't happen during `LAMMPSlib.__init__()`. The object that needs to be passed to the _lammps_ (not ASE) functions doesn't exist until the first call to `calculate`. Without a serious refactor of `LAMMPSlib` this can't be avoided. If you really want to register an arbitrary initializer in `LAMMPSlib.__init__` we can, but it still can't actually be called until the first `calculate`, because `calculate` calls `propagate` which calls `self.start_lammps()` which calls `lammps.lammps()`, which creates the relevant object.

Frankly, if you think calling these functions more than once is bad, the only solution is to have a global (python package or class attribute) flag: it wouldn't be impossible for script to create multiple LAMMPSlib calculators during its run, so having it happen once per calculator construction is already too many times.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
The example is not literal because I the maintainer cannot spend infinite time investigating it, hence ` # or similar`.  The goal is for the user to define a callback and pass the callback, and the Lammps object then calls it at the right time.

I didn't say it should be *called* from inside the constructor.  It is *passed* to the constructor, and called when *necessary*, once the required objects exist and can be passed to the callback function.  Standard callback pattern.

comments.author: noambern
comments.body:
While of course you cannot spend "infinite time" investigating it, you can at least try to use the actual ASE class names if you're referring to the ASE class, so the people you're communicating with can understand, unambiguously, what you're referring to.  `Lammps` is not defined anywhere I can see. The ASE calculator class is `LAMMPSlib` and the lammps-API class is `lammps`.

Anyway, I'll do this callback pattern because you asked, but I don't understand why you think this design solves the problem you are worried about, which from what I can tell is mainly having these linking functions be called multiple times.
